newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda coffee exports dip in February, earnings up.
newsitem.headline: Uganda coffee exports dip in February, earnings up.

text.p: Uganda's coffee exports dropped to 496,378 60-kg bags worth $39.82 million in February from 551,688 bags worth $38.56 million in January, the state-run Uganda Coffee Development Authority (UCDA) said.
UCDA said in a report sent to Reuters on Wednesday that the increase in value reflected the rise seen in international prices since the second week of January.
The unit value of exports in February rose to $1.34 per kg from $1.16 registered in January, UCDA figures showed.
Compared with February last year, the volume and value of exports eased by 4.98 percent and 13.09 percent respectively.
In February, prices paid to farmers rose sharply in response to world price movements.
The average price for kiboko rose from 500 shillings per kg in January to between 600 and 700 at the end of February.
FAQ (fair average quality) ranged between 1,300 and 1,450 shillings as compared to 1,100-1,200 in January. Arabica parchment rose to 1,600-1,700 from 1,300-1,400 in January.

UCDA projected March exports at 401,066 bags worth $32.62 million, with total expectations for the second 1996/97 quarter at 1,449,132 bags worth $110,999,996. This would compare with 1,513,025 bags worth $138,021,551 in the same period last season.
In February, 94 percent of coffee exports were handled by 22 exporters. Nsamba Works Ltd still took the lead with 81,062 bags, or 16.3 percent of the market, UCDA said.
